key_insight: A convolutional-network + attention pipeline can classify intracranial pressure (ICP) cardiac cycles by body position while highlighting interpretable waveform regions, enabling automated feature discovery in ICP monitoring data.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of interpretable, automated feature discovery in intracranial pressure waveform analysis—reducing reliance on manual inspection and enabling localization of waveform regions relevant to physiologic state (body position).
method: Assemble ICP monitoring dataset from 60 patients and segment continuous signals into individual cardiac cycles.
Train a convolutional neural network to classify each cardiac cycle into one of seven body positions.
Extract neural-network attention maps to identify and visualize waveform regions of interest for interpretation and downstream analysis.
impact: Provides a reproducible, interpretable framework for feature discovery in time-series biomedical signals, improving model transparency and enabling AI/ML practitioners to localize meaningful physiological features for validation and further study.
visual_elements: Example ICP waveform with overlaid attention heatmap highlighting regions that drive classification
Pipeline diagram: raw signal → cycle segmentation → CNN classifier → attention extraction → feature localization
Confusion matrix or bar chart showing classification performance across the seven body positions
Aggregated attention heatmap across patients/cycles to reveal cohort-level salient waveform features
paper_title: A Framework for Feature Discovery in Intracranial Pressure Monitoring Data Using Neural Network Attention
paper_authors: Jonathan D. Socha, Seyed F. Maroufi, Dipankar Biswas, Richard Um, Aruna S. Rao
